Definition
[geodesic at a point; totally geodesic immersion]

Source: docarmo:page-0147 ↗ def:dc-ch6-2-2

An immersion $f:M\to \overline{M}$ is geodesic at $p\in M$ if for every $\eta \in (T_pM)^\perp $ the second fundamental form $\mathit{II}_\eta $ is identically zero at $p$ — equivalently, by polarization, $B$ vanishes at $p$. An immersion is totally geodesic if it is geodesic at every $p\in M$.
